S01.title: SF Rent Board · 2026 annual announcement
S01.verified_scope: 1.6% from 2026-03-01 through 2027-02-28; annual formula is base rent × 0.016.

S03.title: SF Rent Board · rent increases
S03.verified_scope: Base rent, 12-month timing, license, written notice, mail, additional occupants and no rounding up. Two examples have conflicting years; see review.

S04.title: SF Rent Board · banking
S04.verified_scope: Skipped increase requires 24 full months without an increase; partial unused increase may be banked; sum eligible rates without compounding or proration. Example has inconsistent year.

S05.title: SF Rent Ordinance § 37.3
S05.verified_scope: Annual, banking, additional occupants, notice disclosure, partial changes, petitions, and cost-related increases.

S06.title: SF Rent Board · coverage
S06.verified_scope: Many pre-June 14, 1979 units are covered; special cases and exemptions; the building must be verified individually.

S07.title: SF Rent Board · housing inventory
S07.verified_scope: Annual and banked increases need a current license in effect by the notice effective date; a license is not itself legal clearance.

S08.title: SF Rent Board · AB 1482
S08.verified_scope: 8.8% for covered AB 1482 units, Aug 1 2026–Jul 31 2027; not a replacement for more protective local limits.

S09.title: California Civil Code § 827
S09.verified_scope: For covered periodic tenancies: personal or mail service, 30 days for ≤10% and 90 for >10%, measured with prior 12-month increases; exceptions and longer rules may apply.

S10.title: California Code of Civil Procedure § 1013
S10.verified_scope: Mail extension is 5 calendar days where both mailing and address are in California; other scenarios differ.

S11.title: California DRE · fixed-term leases
S11.verified_scope: A landlord generally cannot raise rent during a fixed term unless the agreement expressly allows it.

S12.title: SF Rent Board · § 6.14 and Costa-Hawkins
S12.verified_scope: Original occupant remaining, later occupants, timing of 6.14 notices, and co-tenant versus subtenant distinctions require legal review.

S13.title: California Civil Rights Department · housing
S13.verified_scope: State fair-housing protected characteristics, reasonable disability accommodation and retaliation protections.

S14.title: SF Rent Ordinance § 37.9
S14.verified_scope: Subsection (d) prohibits rent increases where the dominant motive is retaliation for exercising legal rights.

S15.title: California Civil Code § 1942.5
S15.verified_scope: Retaliation and tenant-association protections, subject to stated statutory conditions.

S16.title: SF Mayor’s Office · tenant and landlord resources
S16.verified_scope: Counseling for a rent increase notice; free legal assistance for tenants with eviction court papers; landlord resources.

S17.title: SF Rent Board · free counseling
S17.verified_scope: Counseling is free and multilingual; counselors cannot give legal advice.

S18.title: SF Rent Board · unlawful rent petition
S18.verified_scope: Eligible tenants can petition over an alleged unlawful increase or request review of lawful rent; no filing charge.

S19.title: SF Rent Ordinance § 37.10C
S19.verified_scope: Narrowly defined rental-pricing devices using non-public competitor data are prohibited; not a ban on every algorithm.

S20.title: US GAO · institutional investment
S20.verified_scope: Single-family investor studies reviewed; rent effects may exist, but effects on tenants are unclear and not a local owner-by-owner comparison.

S21.title: US DOJ · proposed RealPage settlement
S21.verified_scope: 2025 proposed settlement and complaint allegations concerning rental-pricing software; proposal, not a finding about all landlords.

S22.title: SF Rent Board · landlord petitions
S22.verified_scope: Some increases require filing before notice and approval; some passthroughs use other procedures and worksheets.

S23.title: HUD · Fair Housing Act
S23.verified_scope: Federal protected categories and nondiscrimination in rental housing.

S24.title: California Civil Code § 1942.4
S24.verified_scope: A rent-increase notice is barred when all stated serious-habitability conditions are met; not every repair issue triggers the statute.

S25.title: SF Rent Board · comparables petition
S25.verified_scope: Extraordinary circumstances and comparable rents must be proved; a mere market-rent gap is not an extraordinary circumstance.

S26.title: Congressional Research Service · federal rental programs
S26.verified_scope: Federal rental programs can subsidize rents or impose affordability requirements; unit participation is unknown.

S27.title: SF Rent Board · § 6.14 petition
S27.verified_scope: The Rent Board describes optional landlord determination and tenant challenge; the exceptions and occupancy distinctions are fact-specific.

S28.title: SF Rent Board · Part VI rules
S28.verified_scope: Section 6.14 defines an original occupant and the conditions on subsequent occupants; operating and maintenance petitions have specific requirements.
